VERDICT: ACCEPT

The genus-6 construction checks out. The $(\mathbb Z/2)^2$-cover branched at the 9 points of $B_1\cup B_2$ has Riemann–Hurwitz genus $2g-2=-8+9\cdot 2=10$, so $g=6$, matching $g(C_1)+g(C_2)+g(C_3)=6$. The projections $X\to C_i\hookrightarrow A_i$ are non-constant, so the image curve has both projections non-constant.

The lower bound is the weak point. Surjectivity $JX\twoheadrightarrow A_1\times A_2$ gives $g\ge 4$, and the claim that $g=4,5$ is impossible rests on a dimension count that is only sketched. The most natural genus-5 family, the $(\mathbb Z/2)^2$-cover with quotient genera $(2,2,1)$, does have 5 moduli: it requires $|B_1\cap B_2|=4$, a codimension-1 condition on pairs of genus-2 curves. That supports the heuristic, but I did not verify that every other genus-4 or genus-5 configuration is excluded. I am also not certain of the literature value, so my confidence is modest.

CONFIDENCE: 2
